proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(\delta=2^{-p_n-1}\), and let \(\mathcal B\) be the coordinate box of radius \(\delta\) about \((\widetilde X,\widetilde R,\widetilde C)\). We construct the certificate and verify each assertion.

First, there is a computable coarse enclosure which is valid even when no singular subspace can be separated. Let \(T\) be a directed-rounding upper bound for the absolute values of all coordinates in \(\mathcal B\). At any point of \(\mathcal B\) at which \(G_n\) holds, the retained inverse \(Y=X_r^+\) obeys
\[
\|Y\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\|D_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le \frac{2}{cn}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\|Z_{p,n}\|_2\le \frac{\sqrt nT}{\sigma},\qquad
\|Z_{q,n}\|_2\le \frac{\sqrt nT}{\sigma},\qquad
t_{Z,n}\le \overline t:=\frac{\sqrt{2n}T}{\sigma}.
\]
The last inequality follows because every singular value of \(D_n/\|D_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\) is at most one. Since \(\beta_\alpha(t)\) is decreasing, \(\zeta_\alpha(t)\) is decreasing and hence
\[
0<\zeta_\alpha(t)\le z_{\max}:=\Phi^{-1}(1-3\alpha/8).
\]
Define
\[
\overline R=\sqrt{C_{r,\alpha}\log(e+2\overline t+A_{r,\alpha})}
\]
and
\[
\overline W=\frac{2}{cn}
\left\{z_{\max}(\overline t+\overline R)
+\frac{C_{r,\alpha}}{2}\log(e+\overline t+\overline R)\right\}.
\]
The definitions of \(R_{0,n},t_{-,n},t_{+,n}\) then give \(W_n\le\overline W\). Also
\[
|\widehat\theta_n|=|RYC|\le \frac{2T^2}{c}
\]
and
\[
d_n\le \overline d:=K_0\sigma^2\ell_n n^{-2}
\left(\frac{\sqrt nT}{\sigma}+\sqrt{\ell_n}\right)^2.
\]
Consequently every on-gate exact interval in \(\mathcal B\) lies in
\[
[-\overline H,\overline H],\qquad
\overline H:=\frac{2T^2}{c}+\sigma^2\overline W+\overline d,
\]
whereas every off-gate interval equals \([-M_0,M_0]\). Thus the outward hull of these two displayed intervals is a valid finite fallback for every point in the box. This observation is what makes termination independent of a spectral gap.

We next describe the sharp branch. For a particular matrix \(X\), let
\[
P_R={\bf 1}_{(\tau,\infty)}(X^{\top}X),\qquad
P_L={\bf 1}_{(\tau,\infty)}(XX^{\top}),
\]
where a certified rational \(\tau\) lies strictly between the squared retained and discarded singular values. When the certified count above \(\tau\) is \(r\),
\[
X_r=P_LXP_R,
\qquad
X_r^+=X_r^{\top}\bigl(X_rX_r^{\top}+I-P_L\bigr)^{-1}.
\tag{1}
\]
Indeed, in any compact singular-value decomposition, the inverse on the range of \(P_L\) has eigenvalues \(s_j(X)^{-2}\), while the inverse on its orthogonal complement is the identity; multiplication by \(X_r^{\top}\) proves (1).

Both projectors can be enclosed without choosing individual singular vectors. For example, put \(H_R=X^{\top}X-\tau I\), scale it by a certified power of two \(a\ge\|H_R\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), and apply the matrix-sign iteration
\[
S_0=H_R/a,\qquad S_{j+1}=\frac12(S_j+S_j^{-1}).
\tag{2}
\]
For a nonzero scalar eigenvalue \(x\), the Cayley ratio \((x-\operatorname{sign}(x))/(x+\operatorname{sign}(x))\) is squared by one step of (2). Hence, whenever a signed spectral gap has been certified, (2) converges geometrically and then quadratically to \(\operatorname{sign}(H_R)\), and
\[
P_R=\frac12\{I+\operatorname{sign}(H_R)\}.
\]
The same construction yields \(P_L\). Every inverse in (1) and (2) is accepted only after a directed residual enclosure proves \(\|I-K\widetilde K^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}<1\); the Neumann identity
\[
K^{-1}=\widetilde K^{-1}
\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}(I-K\widetilde K^{-1})^j
\]
then gives a rigorous outward error bound. If the residual test or the spectral count is not certified by the prescribed precision cap, the algorithm takes the coarse branch. Thus failure to resolve a zero or extremely small gap cannot cause nontermination.

Equations (1)--(2) depend only on the whole retained invariant subspaces. A repeated singular value inside the retained block changes neither \(P_L\), \(P_R\), nor \(X_r^+\). Furthermore, all quantities used by the exact interval are invariant under an orthogonal change of retained singular-vector basis, because
\[
\widehat\theta_n=RX_r^+C,qquad
s_{Z,n}=\sigma^{-1}
\sqrt{\|X_r^+C\|_2^2+\|(X_r^+)^{\top}R^{\top}\|_2^2},
\]
and
\[
\|Z_{p,n}\|_2=\|P_RR^{\top}\|_2/\sigma,qquad
\|Z_{q,n}\|_2=\|P_LC\|_2/\sigma.
\]
This proves validity at repeated retained singular values. A tie across the retained/discarded boundary is sent to the coarse branch, which contains the value selected by every fixed measurable convention.

All scalar functions can also be enclosed constructively. The identities
\[
\Phi(x)=\frac12+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}
\int_0^x e^{-t^2/2}\,dt
\]
and, by radial integration in \(2r\) dimensions,
\[
F_{\chi^2_{2r}}(x)=1-e^{-x/2}
\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}\frac{(x/2)^j}{j!},\qquad x\ge0,
\tag{3}
\]
reduce their evaluation to rational arithmetic, exponentials, and square roots. The exponential series with a remainder bounded by the first omitted absolute tail, after binary range reduction, and Newton enclosures for square roots give directed intervals of \(s\) bits in a number of bit operations polynomial in \(s\) and the binary encoding length of the argument. For the normal quantile, the exponential-moment inequality
\[
1-\Phi(x)\le e^{-x^2/2},\qquad x\ge0,
\]
gives a bracket of size \(O(\sqrt{1+\log(1/\alpha)})\). For the chi-square quantile at tail probability \(\gamma\), (3) gives a bracket of size
\[
O_{r_0}\bigl(1+\log(1/\gamma)\bigr).
\]
On the relevant brackets, the densities are positive. Bisection, with the function-evaluation precision increased whenever a comparison interval contains the target probability, therefore returns an interval of width at most
\[
8\,2^{1-q_n}(1+|Q|)
\]
around either requested quantile \(Q\). The required extra probability bits are at most a constant multiple of \(q_n+\log(1/\alpha)+\log(1+t)\): this follows directly from the normal density and, in (3), from the factor \(e^{-x/2}\). Binary range reduction stores the possibly large scale in the arbitrary-precision exponent, so its cost is polynomial in the encoding length of that exponent, not in its numerical value.

For non-dyadic public controls, the refinable name is queried to the additional precision demanded by the preceding comparison tests. A fixed, nonrefinable interval would not suffice: with \(r=1\), \(F_{\chi^2_2}^{-1}(1-\gamma)=-2\log\gamma\), so an interval allowing \(\gamma\) to range from \(2^{-2^L}\) to a fixed positive number has endpoint encoding length \(O(L)\) but an unboundedly growing quantile image. This proves the necessity of the representation clause in the proposed statement.

Choose a cap
\[
q_n^\star=8\bigl(n+L_n+p_n+\lceil\log_2(1/\alpha)\rceil+1\bigr)^2.
\]
At successively doubled precisions no larger than \(q_n^\star\), the algorithm tries to certify that every matrix in the box is off the gate, or that every matrix is on the gate with a common retained spectral split. In the first case it returns the outward-rounded fallback. In the second it evaluates (1) and all endpoint formulas by directed arithmetic. In every other case it returns the coarse hull already proved valid. The number of matrix operations is polynomial in \(n\); (2), whenever used, takes polynomially many iterations; and every mantissa and dynamically stored exponent has polynomial encoding length. Hence termination and bit complexity are polynomial in the quantities asserted in the statement.

Finally, let \([L(X,R,C),U(X,R,C)]\) be an exact-real interval for a point in the box and let \([\underline L,\overline U]\) be the returned interval. Directed evaluation gives
\[
\underline L\le L(X,R,C)\le U(X,R,C)\le\overline U.
\]
Assign to \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\) the outward endpoint displacement caused by replacing a point by its coordinate and control boxes, including a gate hull caused by those boxes, and assign to \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}\) the additional nonnegative radii from (1)--(3), scalar evaluation, gate classification at finite precision, and endpoint rounding. The construction gives, endpoint by endpoint,
\[
0\le L-\underline L\le\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}},
\qquad
0\le\overline U-U\le\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}.
\]
Adding the two inequalities proves
\[
0\le \operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{dyad}})
-\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}(X,R,C))
\le2(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}).
\]
Arbitrary-precision signed exponents exclude overflow and subnormal numbers by definition. An IEEE implementation is accepted only after exact power-of-two rescaling and rejection of every overflow, subnormal, or flush flag, as required by the directed-rounding model. This completes the deterministic certificate.

theorem.statement:
A single nonrefinable dyadic interval for a public control does not suffice for the requested quantile-width certificate. Under the exact-dyadic or polynomial-time refinable control representation in the corrected deterministic certificate, however, the answer to the question is affirmative. Put
\[
h_\alpha=\lceil\log_2(64/\alpha)\rceil,
\qquad
g_n=20\{h_\alpha+\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil+1\},
\]
\[
p_n=n^2+4g_n,qquad q_n=p_n-g_n,qquad
\tau_n=B+\sigma\sqrt{12\log(e+n)}+1,
\]
and, for a sufficiently large fixed integer \(C_\star\),
\[
L_n=p_n+\lceil\log_2(p_n+2)\rceil
+\lceil\log_2\tau_n\rceil+2g_n+C_\star.
\]
Then \(p_n,L_n,q_n\) are polynomially bounded in \(n\) and \(\lceil\log_2(1/\alpha)\rceil\), \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\ge\tau_n\), and the composed measurable interval \(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\) satisfies
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
P\{\theta_n\in I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\}\ge1-\alpha,
\qquad
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P(\kappa_n=1)=o(n^{-1}),
\]
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
\frac{\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_n]}{w_n}\longrightarrow0,
\qquad
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
\frac{\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}})]}{w_n}
\le K_\alpha.
\]
On \(\kappa_n=0\),
\[
I_n^{\mathrm{out}}(X,R,C)\subseteq I_n^{\mathrm{fp}},
\qquad
0\le\varepsilon_n\le2\Delta_n^{\mathrm{num}};
\]
on \(\kappa_n=1\), \(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}=[-M_0,M_0]\). Along every sequence \(P_n\in\mathcal P_n\) with \(b_n/a_n\to0\),
\[
\frac{\varepsilon_n}{a_n}\longrightarrow0
\quad\hbox{in \(L^1(P_n)\) and in probability},
\qquad
\frac{\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}})}
{2\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)a_n}\longrightarrow1
\quad\hbox{in probability}.
\]
Finally, uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), the expectation of every nonnegative recorded summand of \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\) and \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}\), the fallback contribution \(M_0\mathbf 1\{\kappa_n=1\}\), and \(\varepsilon_n\) is \(o(n^{-1})\). In particular this holds along every sequence with \(r=1\) and \(u=v=0\).
theorem.proof_tex:
We first verify the schedules and encoding. From the definition of \(L_n\),
\[
T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}
=2^{L_n-p_n-\lceil\log_2(p_n+2)\rceil-4}
=2^{\lceil\log_2\tau_n\rceil+2g_n+C_\star-4}
\ge\tau_n
\]
when \(C_\star\ge4\). It is also bounded by a fixed polynomial in \(n\) and \(\alpha^{-1}\), times \(1+\sqrt{\log(e+n)}\). If \(\kappa_n=0\), rounding a coordinate \(x\) produces an integer numerator of at most
\[
p_n+\lceil\log_2(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1)\rceil+2
\]
bits, and the signed exponent \(-p_n\) uses \(O(\log(p_n+2))\) bits. The choice of \(L_n\), after increasing the fixed \(C_\star\), therefore places every rounded coordinate in \(\mathbb D_{L_n}\). The refinable names of the finitely many public controls are requested at precision \(p_n+g_n\); their endpoint descriptions also fit within \(L_n\). All three schedules are polynomial in the asserted arguments.

There are \(N_n=n^2+2n\le3n^2\) observed coordinates, and every corresponding mean is bounded by \(B\). If \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), exponential Markov inequalities applied to \(e^{tZ}\) and \(e^{-tZ}\) give
\[
P(|Z|>x)\le2e^{-x^2/2},\qquad x\ge0.
\tag{9}
\]
Since \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\ge B+\sigma\sqrt{12\ell_n}+1\), a union bound and (9) give
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P(\kappa_n=1)
\le 2N_ne^{-6\ell_n}
\le6n^2(e+n)^{-6}=O(n^{-4})=o(n^{-1}).
\tag{10}
\]

We next isolate the stable donor event without invoking an undeclared tail theorem. A maximal \(1/4\)-separated subset of the Euclidean unit sphere has cardinality at most \(9^n\), by comparing the disjoint balls of radius \(1/8\) with a ball of radius \(9/8\). For such nets \(\mathcal N_1,\mathcal N_2\), approximation of both unit vectors gives
\[
\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2\max_{x\in\mathcal N_1,y\in\mathcal N_2}|x^{\top}Ey|.
\]
Each \(x^{\top}Ey/\sigma\) is standard normal. Thus (9) and a union bound imply
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P\{\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}>cn/8\}
\le2\,9^{2n}\exp\left(-\frac{c^2n^2}{512\sigma^2}\right)
\le e^{-k_0n^2}
\tag{11}
\]
for some \(k_0>0\) and all sufficiently large \(n\).

On the event in which \(\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le cn/8\), Weyl's singular-value inequality follows from
\[
\|Xz\|_2\le\|Az\|_2+\|Ez\|_2,qquad
\|Az\|_2\le\|Xz\|_2+\|Ez\|_2,
\]
and the min--max characterization. Hence
\[
s_r(X)\ge7cn/8,qquad s_{r+1}(X)\le cn/8,qquad
s_1(X)\le C_0n+cn/8.
\tag{12}
\]
The true data and every point in its rounded coordinate box differ entrywise by at most \(2^{-p_n}\), and therefore differ in operator norm by at most \(n2^{-p_n}\). For all sufficiently large \(n\), (12) consequently implies, throughout that box,
\[
s_r\ge3cn/4,qquad s_{r+1}\le cn/4,qquad s_1\le3C_0n/2.
\tag{13}
\]

Let
\[
P_n^\star=K_\star(n+T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\alpha^{-1}+1)^{k_\star}.
\]
On \(\kappa_n=0\), the coordinate box is bounded by \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1\). The stable-padding lemma, (11), and (13) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
\mathbb E_P\bigl[(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}})
\mathbf 1\{\kappa_n=0\}\bigr]
&\le P_n^\star(2^{-p_n}+2^{1-q_n})
+P_n^\star e^{-k_0n^2}\\
&=o(n^{-m})
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
\]
for every fixed \(m>0\). Here \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\) and \(P_n^\star\) grow only polynomially, whereas \(p_n\) and \(q_n\) equal \(n^2+O(\log n+\log(1/\alpha))\). Because all recorded summands are nonnegative, (14) holds with the sum replaced by any one of them.

The deterministic certificate gives, on \(\kappa_n=0\),
\[
I_n^{\mathrm{out}}(X,R,C)\subseteq I_n^{\mathrm{fp}},
\qquad
0\le\varepsilon_n\le2(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}})
=2\Delta_n^{\mathrm{num}}.
\tag{15}
\]
On \(\kappa_n=1\), the procedure returns \([-M_0,M_0]\). This interval always contains the target, because
\[
|\theta_n|=|uA^+v|
\le\|u\|_2\|A^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|v\|_2
\le (B\sqrt n)\frac{1}{cn}(B\sqrt n)=M_0.
\tag{16}
\]
The numerical records are set to zero when the handle is not run, and the fallback is recorded separately. Since interval lengths are nonnegative, the definition of \(\varepsilon_n\) also gives \(0\le\varepsilon_n\le2M_0\) on \(\kappa_n=1\). Equations (10), (14), and (15) imply
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_n]=o(n^{-1}),
\qquad
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
\mathbb E_P[M_0\mathbf 1\{\kappa_n=1\}]=o(n^{-1}).
\tag{17}
\]
They also prove the stated summand-by-summand assertion, including the joint-zero rank-one case.

Containment in (15) and validity of (16) show, pointwise,
\[
\{\theta_n\in I_n^{\mathrm{out}}\}
\subseteq\{\theta_n\in I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\}.
\]
The already established uniform coverage theorem for \(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}\) therefore proves
\[
\liminf_n\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
P\{\theta_n\in I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\}\ge1-\alpha.
\tag{18}
\]

The transition scale has the uniform lower bound
\[
w_n\ge b_n=\sigma^2\|A^+\|_{\mathrm F}
\ge\frac{\sigma^2}{s_1(A)}
\ge\frac{\sigma^2}{C_0n}.
\tag{19}
\]
Combining (17) and (19) yields
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
\frac{\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_n]}{w_n}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{20}
\]
For any two nonnegative numbers \(x,y\), \(x\le y+[x-y]_+\). Thus
\[
\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}})
\le\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{out}})+\varepsilon_n.
\]
The established transition-length theorem and (20) give the claimed \(K_\alpha\) upper bound.

Finally, suppose \(b_n/a_n\to0\). By (19), \(na_n\to\infty\). The uniform statement in (17) gives
\[
\frac{\mathbb E_{P_n}[\varepsilon_n]}{a_n}
=\frac{n\mathbb E_{P_n}[\varepsilon_n]}{na_n}\longrightarrow0,
\]
so \(\varepsilon_n/a_n\to0\) in \(L^1(P_n)\) and in probability. On \(\kappa_n=0\), (15) makes the length difference nonnegative and no larger than \(\varepsilon_n\); on \(\kappa_n=1\), the exceptional probability tends to zero by (10). Therefore
\[
\frac{\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}})
-\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{out}})}{a_n}
\longrightarrow0
\]
in probability. For every \(\varepsilon>0\), the probability that the normalized finite-precision length differs from one by more than \(\varepsilon\) is bounded by the sum of the probabilities that the exact-real normalized length differs from one by more than \(\varepsilon/2\) and that the normalized length difference exceeds \(\varepsilon/2\). Both terms tend to zero by the preceding display and the established oracle-length theorem for \(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}\). This gives the asserted oracle Gaussian length for \(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\).

For completeness, the first sentence of the theorem is forced rather than cosmetic. If \(r=1\), \(t=0\), and a one-shot control interval permits \(\alpha\) to range from \(2^{-2^L}\) to \(1/4\), then
\[
F_{\chi^2_2}^{-1}(1-\alpha/4)=-2\log(\alpha/4)
\]
ranges over an interval whose width is of order \(2^L\), although the control endpoints have encoding length \(O(L)\). At the fixed endpoint \(\alpha=1/4\), the required tolerance is at most \(8(1+|Q|)\) for every \(q_n\ge1\), a constant. No algorithm receiving only that one-shot interval can meet the requested quantile-width guarantee. Exact controls or refinable certified names remove precisely this information-theoretic obstruction, and the preceding construction proves all remaining claims.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\delta_n=2^{-p_n-1}\), and, on \(\kappa_n=0\), let \(\mathcal B_n\) be the coordinate box of radius \(\delta_n\) about \((\widetilde X,\widetilde R,\widetilde C)\). The certificate in \(H_n^{\mathrm{cert}}\) can be chosen so that there are finite constants \(K_\star\) and \(k_\star\), depending only on \(c,C_0,B,\sigma,r_0\), for which the following holds for all sufficiently large \(n>r_0\). If every coordinate of the box is at most \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1\) in absolute value, then
\[
0\le\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}
\le K_\star(n+T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\alpha^{-1}+1)^{k_\star}.
\]
If in addition every donor matrix \(X'\) in the box satisfies
\[
s_r(X')\ge3cn/4,\qquad s_{r+1}(X')\le cn/4,
\qquad s_1(X')\le3C_0n/2,
\]
then
\[
\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}
\le K_\star(n+T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\alpha^{-1}+1)^{k_\star}
\bigl(2^{-p_n}+2^{1-q_n}\bigr).
\]
Every nonnegative radius recorded as a summand of either \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\) or \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}\) obeys the corresponding upper bound.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The coarse bound in the proof of the deterministic certificate gives the first inequality. Indeed, with \(T=T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1\), the displayed bounds for \(\overline t,\overline R,\overline W,\overline d\), and \(\overline H\) are bounded by a fixed polynomial in \(n,T,\alpha^{-1}+1\); logarithms and square roots are bounded by one plus their arguments. The fallback radius \(M_0=B^2/c\) is fixed. The certificate never needs to record a radius larger than the diameter of the resulting coarse hull plus one final rounding unit. This proves the global polynomial bound.

For the sharp bound, set \(\tau=(cn/2)^2\). The assumed singular-value inequalities give, for both \(X'^{\top}X'\) and \(X'X'^{\top}\), a separation from \(\tau\) of at least
\[
\min\left\{(3cn/4)^2-(cn/2)^2,
(cn/2)^2-(cn/4)^2\right\}
=\frac{3c^2n^2}{16}.
\tag{4}
\]
For two matrices \(X_1,X_2\) in the box,
\[
\|X_1^{\top}X_1-X_2^{\top}X_2\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le(\|X_1\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\|X_2\|_{\mathrm{op}})
\|X_1-X_2\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le K n\|X_1-X_2\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{5}
\]
Let \(\Gamma\) be a rectangular contour lying in the gap (4) and enclosing the retained squared singular values. The resolvent identity gives
\[
P_R(X_1)-P_R(X_2)
=\frac{1}{2\pi\mathrm i}\int_\Gamma
(z-X_1^{\top}X_1)^{-1}
(X_1^{\top}X_1-X_2^{\top}X_2)
(z-X_2^{\top}X_2)^{-1}\,dz.
\]
The contour has length \(O(n^2)\), while both resolvents are \(O(n^{-2})\) by (4). Combining this fact with (5) yields
\[
\|P_R(X_1)-P_R(X_2)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le K\frac{\|X_1-X_2\|_{\mathrm{op}}}{n}.
\tag{6}
\]
The same bound holds for \(P_L\). Applying the ordinary inverse identity
\[
K_1^{-1}-K_2^{-1}=K_1^{-1}(K_2-K_1)K_2^{-1}
\]
to formula (1) in the preceding proof, using \(s_r(X_j)\ge3cn/4\), gives
\[
\|X_{1,r}^+-X_{2,r}^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le K\frac{\|X_1-X_2\|_{\mathrm{op}}}{n^2}.
\tag{7}
\]
These derivations use a projector onto the entire retained cluster and therefore do not require distinct retained singular values.

Across the coordinate box,
\[
\|X_1-X_2\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2n\delta_n,qquad
\|R_1-R_2\|_2\le2\sqrt n\delta_n,qquad
\|C_1-C_2\|_2\le2\sqrt n\delta_n.
\tag{8}
\]
The invariant formulas
\[
RX_r^+C,quad \|X_r^+\|_{\mathrm{op}},quad
\sigma^{-1}\sqrt{\|X_r^+C\|_2^2+\|(X_r^+)^{\top}R^{\top}\|_2^2},
\quad \|P_RR^{\top}\|_2/\sigma,quad \|P_LC\|_2/\sigma
\]
together with (6)--(8) show that their total variation over the box is at most
\[
K(n+T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1)^k2^{-p_n}
\]
for fixed \(K,k\). On the stable set,
\[
\frac{2}{3C_0n}\le\|X_r^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\frac{4}{3cn},
\]
so division by \(h_n=\|X_r^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\) introduces only a polynomial factor. The arguments of every logarithm and square root in \(W_n\) are bounded away from zero. The derivative of \(\zeta_\alpha\) is also polynomially bounded in \(\alpha^{-1}\): if \(z=\Phi^{-1}(1-q)\) with \(3\alpha/8\le q\le\alpha/2\), then
\[
q=\int_z^\infty\phi(x)\,dx\le\frac{\phi(z)}{z},
\]
and \(z\) is bounded away from zero because \(q<1/4\). Hence \(1/\phi(z)\le K/\alpha\). The maps \(x\mapsto\max\{0,x\}\) and \(x\mapsto\|x\|_2\) are one-Lipschitz. It follows by composition that the encoding contribution is bounded by
\[
K_\star(n+T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\alpha^{-1}+1)^{k_\star}2^{-p_n}.
\]

In directed \(q_n\)-bit arithmetic, a polynomial number of operations contributes at most a polynomial condition factor times \(2^{1-q_n}\). The residual tests for the matrix-sign and inverse steps are uniformly successful under (4), and the scalar quantile bisections have the positive-density bounds established in the deterministic proof. Therefore the arithmetic contribution is bounded by
\[
K_\star(n+T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\alpha^{-1}+1)^{k_\star}2^{1-q_n}.
\]
Increasing \(K_\star,k_\star\) once gives the asserted sum. Since all recorded radii are nonnegative and their sum is \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}\), each individual summand satisfies the same bound.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Assume that every public real control is represented either by an exact dyadic number or by a polynomial-time refinable dyadic name of original description length at most \(L_n\): on input \(s\), the name returns a certified dyadic interval containing that control, of width at most \(2^{-s}\), whose endpoint encoding lengths and computation time are polynomial in \(s\) and \(L_n\). For every exact dyadic triple \((\widetilde X,\widetilde R,\widetilde C)\) in \(\mathbb D_{L_n}^{n^2+2n}\), every real triple \((X,R,C)\) in its coordinate box of radius \(2^{-p_n-1}\), and public controls with the preceding representation, there is a working precision \(q_n\) bounded by a polynomial in \(n,L_n,p_n,\lceil\log_2(1/\alpha)\rceil\) such that \(H_n^{\mathrm{cert}}\) terminates in bit complexity polynomial in the same quantities and returns \(I_n^{\mathrm{dyad}}\) containing the exact-real interval \(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}(X,R,C)\). The certificate gives
\[
0\le \operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{dyad}})-\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}(X,R,C))
\le 2(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}).
\]
It remains valid for repeated retained singular values, computes outward enclosures of \(\Phi^{-1}\) and \(F_{\chi^2_{2r}}^{-1}\) in certified polynomial time, returns the bounded outward fallback hull whenever the spectral gate or the retained/discarded spectral split is uncertain, and never silently accepts overflow, a subnormal value, or flush-to-zero behavior.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: A single nonrefinable control interval can encode values of the miscoverage level arbitrarily close to zero and bounded away from zero simultaneously. For two chi-square degrees of freedom its admissible quantiles then have arbitrarily large spread, so no enclosure can satisfy the frozen relative-width requirement. Exact dyadic controls or polynomial-time refinable dyadic names are the minimal information-model repair; they do not assume the spectral or statistical crux.
